[[File:Yabu-jinja, entrance.jpg|thumb|250px|{{center|Precinct entrance}}]]
{{nihongo|'''Yabu Shrine'''|養父神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Ichiba, {{ill|Yabu, Hyōgo|Q869014|qid=Q869014}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is the {{ill|Tajima Province|Q1053727|qid=Q1053727}} {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=third-ranking provincial shrine (sannomiya)}}, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (2 myōjin-taisha seats and 3 small-shrine seats), and under the former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} system it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}. {{nihongo|'''Yabu Shrine'''|養父神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tajima Province]].

It is popularly called "Yabu no Myojin-san" and is known as a deity of agriculture. Ichiba in Yabu has long been a center of cattle markets for {{ill|Tajima cattle|Q13417172|qid=Q13417172}}, and auctions are still held at nearby Ōyabu.

== Enshrined deities ==
The five currently enshrined seats are:
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōanamuji-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tanba Michinushi-no-Mikoto}}
* Funahotari-no-Mikoto - descendant of Tanba Michinushi-no-Mikoto and ancestor of the provincial rulers of Tajima
In ''Tajima-kō'', a regional record compiled in the Edo period, it is described that once the upper shrine on Mt. Yadaka enshrined Ōanamuji-no-Mikoto, the middle shrine on the mid-slope enshrined Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto and Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto, and the lower shrine at the present site enshrined Tanba Michinushi-no-Mikoto. ''{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}'' treats four seats other than Ōanamuji as uncertain. ''Yabu Gunshi'' (1928) gives the upper shrine deities as {{ill|Ukemochi|Q2280323|qid=Q2280323}} and {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|lt=Isotakeru|Q10881556|qid=Q10881556}}, the middle shrine as Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto, and the lower shrine as Tanba Michinushi-no-Mikoto and Funahotari-no-Mikoto<ref name="bunken1">''Gods of Japan (7) San'in'', p.331</ref>.

== History ==
Tradition says the shrine was founded in the 30th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوجین|fr|Sujin|hr|Sujin|id|Kaisar Sujin|it|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|ka|სუძინი|ko|스진 천황|ms|Maharaja Sujin|nl|Sujin|pl|Sujin|pt|Sujin|ru|Император Судзин|sh|Car Sujin|simple|Emperor Sujin|sl|Cesar Sudžin|sr|Суџин|sv|Sujin|th|จักรพรรดิซูจิง|tl|Emperador Sujin|tr|Sujin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Судзін|uz|Imperator Sujin|vi|Thiên hoàng Sujin|yo|Emperor Sujin|zh|崇神天皇|zh_classical|崇神天皇|zh_min_nan|Suzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|崇神天皇|qid=Q333530}}, and it is already named together with {{ill|Izushi Shrine|Q3156511|qid=Q3156511}} and {{ill|Awaga Shrine|Q11604651|qid=Q11604651}} in the ''Tajima no Kuni Zeiseichō'' of {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 9 ({{ill|AD 737|Q23583|qid=Q23583}}).

For divine court rank, it received junior fifth rank lower in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 12 (845) (''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}''), rose to senior fifth rank lower in Jōgan 11 (869), and to senior fifth rank upper in Jōgan 16 (874) (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}''). The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' records "Yabufuza Shrine, five seats (two myōjin-tai and three small seats)"<ref name="bunken1" />.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, Suisenzan Fugen-ji served as the attached temple.

In {{ill|1814|Q6943|qid=Q6943}} (Bunka 11), {{ill|Inō Tadataka|Q1240937|qid=Q1240937}} visited during his {{ill|Surveying|Q816425|qid=Q816425}} expedition.

== Cultural properties ==
== Registered cultural properties of Hyogo Prefecture ==
* Tangible cultural properties
** Yabu Shrine, 5 structures (buildings) - registered March 5, 2010 (Heisei 22)<ref>{{Cite web|和書|format=PDF |url=http://www.hyogo-c.ed.jp/~shabun-bo/gyouseisituhp/top/29kentouroku.pdf |title=List of prefecturally registered cultural properties |website=Hyogo Prefectural Education and Training Institute |accessdate=2020-01-13}}</ref>.
*** Main hall - built in the late Edo period.
*** Worship hall - built in the late Edo period.
*** Main hall of Sessha Yamanokuchi Shrine - built in the late Edo period.
*** Main hall of Sessha Gosha Shrine - built in the late Edo period.

== Yabu City designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible cultural properties
** Stone hōkyōintō pagoda - designated May 18, 1977 (Showa 52)<ref>Explanation board for the stone hōkyōintō pagoda.</ref>.
* Intangible folk cultural properties
** Oshiri Festival

== Access ==
* Rail / bus
** About 2 km on foot from {{ill|Yabu Station|Q871175|qid=Q871175}} on the JR {{ill|San'in Main Line|Q1135170|qid=Q1135170}}
** From JR San'in Main Line Yabu Station, take {{ill|Zentan Bus|Q11389110|qid=Q11389110}} bound for "Yōka Station" and get off at "Yabu Myojin"
** From JR San'in Main Line {{ill|Yōka Station|Q870988|qid=Q870988}}, take Zentan Bus bound for "Wadayama / Yamaguchi" and get off at "Yabu Myojin"
* Roads
** About 1 hour from {{ill|Fukuchiyama interchange|Q11594317|qid=Q11594317|lt=Fukuchiyama IC}} on the {{ill|Maizuru-Wakasa Expressway|Q11613730|qid=Q11613730}}
** About 20 minutes from the Asago-side exit of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tōen Tunnel Toll Road}}
** About 15 minutes from {{ill|Wadayama interchange|Q10921611|qid=Q10921611|lt=Wadayama IC}} on the {{ill|Bantan Renraku Road|Q11498699|qid=Q11498699}}
** About 5 minutes from {{ill|Roadside station Yabu|Q11640978|qid=Q11640978}} and {{ill|Roadside station Tajima-rakuza|Q11641146|qid=Q11641146}}
